hero.lead: A nation of 29.9 million with forest over four tenths of its land and two thirds of its power from renewable sources, which completed its IMF programmes in 2025.

register.name: International bond by private placement
register.detail: Ministry of Finance · Arranged 26 January 2026 · Seven years, two years’ grace · 10.125% at arrangement; about 7.79% in euros after the currency swap
register.note: About FCFA 413 billion; offers of nearly $1 billion for $600 million first sought.
register.text: Cameroon’s return to the international market raised $750 million, about FCFA 413 billion, in January 2026. The Ministry of Finance says the proceeds go mainly to clearing payments still due from the previous budget, including works on priority state projects. Every point of interest saved on such debt leaves more of the budget for the seven standards.

register.name: Douala–Bangui Economic Corridor Program, Phase 1
register.detail: World Bank · Board approval 12 June 2026 · IBRD $407M and IDA $18M to Cameroon · Phase 1 of $525M in a $1.12B multiphase program
register.note: Cameroon’s share of Phase 1: $407 million from IBRD and $18 million from IDA (sum, arithmetic).
register.text: A multiphase program to rehabilitate priority sections of the road from Douala to Bangui to climate-resilient standards, with axle-load control stations, logistics hubs and feeder roads. The World Bank says the corridor’s barriers raise consumer prices and undermine food security, and expects about 2,000 to 4,000 direct and indirect jobs. It serves food and livelihood.

register.name: Sustainable Cities and Land Project
register.detail: World Bank · IDA · Release of 30 May 2025 · Yaoundé and Douala
register.note: Expected to reach an estimated 2.1 million people.
register.text: Climate-resilient urban infrastructure in Yaoundé and Douala, technical support for sustainable city development and better land administration services. It is expected to reach an estimated 2.1 million people. It serves shelter.

register.name: Cameroon Water Security Program, Phase 1
register.detail: World Bank · IDA · Approved 7 May 2025 · Phase 1 of a $950M multiphase program, May 2025 to May 2036
register.note: The program is expected to bring drinking water to about 3.9 million people and sanitation to 2.9 million.
register.text: The first of three phases ($200 million, $400 million and $350 million) of a program for water security and sanitation in rural and semi-urban areas of Adamawa, the North and the Far North, and in Yaoundé and Douala, with support for the utility CAMWATER. It serves water and shelter.

register.name: IFC senior loan to Afriland First Bank for small businesses
register.detail: IFC · Yaoundé, 2 April 2025 · $20M from IFC’s own account and $40M mobilized from other lenders · In euros
register.note: Up to $60 million equivalent in euros, with incentives for lending to women-owned or women-led businesses.
register.text: A senior loan from IFC that funds Afriland First Bank’s lending to small and medium enterprises, with a focus on women entrepreneurs, and advice on growing that portfolio. IFC says the partnership will reach thousands of smaller businesses. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Fiscal Sustainability DPF and IMPACT Program-for-Results
register.detail: World Bank · IBRD · Board approval 14 March 2025 · Two operations · The DPF is the second of a 2022–2026 series
register.note: The two operations together: budget support and a Program-for-Results.
register.text: Budget support for inclusive growth, climate resilience and public financial management, with reforms on teacher distribution, girls’ education, social safety nets and the finances of the electricity sector, beside a Program-for-Results to raise domestic revenue and improve basic services such as health care and water supply. It serves education, health, water, energy and livelihood.

register.name: Resilience and Sustainability Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved January 2024 · 18 months · Third and final review 24 July 2025
register.note: SDR 138 million approved; SDR 120.75 million (US$162.3 million) disbursed in all.
register.text: An 18-month arrangement of SDR 138 million (US$181.7 million) for Cameroon’s climate agenda. The third and final review, on 24 July 2025, made SDR 51.75 million (US$71 million) available; the IMF wrote that financing for the uncompleted reform would not become available at expiry. Climate reforms protect the harvests, water and power on which the seven standards rest.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility and Extended Fund Facility
register.detail: IMF · Approved July 2021 · Extended by 12 months in December 2023 · Eighth and final reviews 24 July 2025
register.note: Approved at SDR 483 million (US$689.5 million); SDR 593.4 million (US$793.8 million) disbursed in all.
register.text: Three-year arrangements approved in July 2021 and extended by 12 months, whose eighth and final reviews were completed on 24 July 2025, with total disbursements of SDR 593.4 million (US$793.8 million). Since then the IMF has followed Cameroon through a post-financing assessment, the review for members with IMF credit outstanding and no active programme.

register.name: Electricity Transmission and Reform Project, additional financing
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 13 June 2026
register.text: EUR 43 million more for the national grid, so the power of the new dams reaches homes and factories.

register.name: Enhancing Connectivity and Resilience in the Far North
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 11 June 2026
register.text: Roads and services in the Far North, the region hit hardest by conflict and climate shocks.

register.name: Adaptive Safety Nets and Economic Inclusion Project
register.detail: World Bank · Approved 18 August 2025
register.text: Cash transfers and help to earn a living for the poorest households, ready to scale up when a shock strikes.

register.name: Douala–Bafoussam Road Rehabilitation Project
register.detail: IsDB · Signed in Bangkok, 13 October 2026 · 218 km of national roads and 108 km of feeder roads
register.note: About FCFA 139.2 billion, as reported in the Cameroonian press.
register.text: IsDB financing to rehabilitate the corridor that links the Littoral and West regions to the Port of Douala, with classrooms, health centres, water facilities, markets and agricultural facilities along the road. It serves livelihood, food, education, health and water for the communities on the corridor.

register.name: Agro-Industry in the North, Phase 1 (PDAS-1)
register.detail: African Development Bank · Board approval, release of 14 July 2026 · Total cost €88.74M, with €7.54M from the Government
register.note: Multi-purpose hillside dams in the North and Far North.
register.text: A loan for multi-purpose hillside dams that supply water for farming and livestock in the North and Far North, with hydrometeorological stations, tree planting and community forests. It is expected to raise farm productivity, give water all year and lift household incomes. It serves food, water and livelihood.

register.name: Opening up the East, Phase 1 (PDCBET)
register.detail: African Development Bank · Board approval 18 February 2026 · 156 km of the Ngoura II–Yokadouma road
register.note: At least 2,500 direct and indirect jobs expected.
register.text: A loan to develop and pave 156 kilometres of the Ngoura II to Yokadouma road, on the route from Bertoua to the border with the Republic of Congo. It gives residents, producers and businesses of the East year-round access to production areas and markets, and is expected to create at least 2,500 jobs. It serves livelihood.

register.name: Trade finance for AFG Bank Cameroon
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved 21 October 2026 · Credit line of up to €30M over 3.5 years and a transaction guarantee
register.text: Helps businesses, women and young people above all, import equipment for industry, agro-industry and telecommunications.

register.name: Transaction guarantee for CCA-Bank
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Approved 1 December 2025, Abidjan
register.text: Risk cover so Crédit Communautaire d’Afrique-Bank can finance more trade for small and medium-sized enterprises.

register.name: Skills for Employability and Entrepreneurship in the Far North (CAP2E)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Loan agreements signed 29 September 2025, Yaoundé
register.text: Skills, jobs and modern infrastructure for young people in the conflict-affected Far North.

register.name: Ngaoundéré–Garoua road (PAST4)
register.detail: African Development Bank Group · Signed 19 March 2025, Yaoundé · 246 km of the Douala–N’Djamena corridor
register.text: Rebuilds and widens a key section of the corridor that carries trade from the port of Douala to Chad and the Central African Republic.

register.name: FMO senior loan to AFG Bank Cameroon
register.detail: FMO · Disclosed 1 April 2026 · In contracting · Part of a syndication of up to €65M · EFSD+ guarantee
register.note: Long-term funding for lending to micro, small and medium enterprises.
register.text: FMO approved a €30 million senior loan to give AFG Bank Cameroon long-term funding to expand its lending to the private sector, with a focus on micro, small and medium enterprises. An EFSD+ guarantee supports lending to businesses run by women, young people and migrants. It serves livelihood.

register.name: ARIZ portfolio guarantee for Advans Cameroun
register.detail: Proparco · Signed in Douala, 26 January 2024 · Covers 80% of a FCFA 1.6bn loan portfolio
register.note: About €2 million; one of five Proparco guarantees to Advans Cameroun since 2010.
register.text: A Proparco guarantee that shares the risk on new microfinance loans by Advans Cameroun, mainly to smallholder farmers in rural areas in the maize and broiler chains. Proparco reports access to financial services for 564 beneficiaries. It serves livelihood and food.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Part of the Congo Basin, the second lung of the planet: carbon and timber that can earn as they stand.
items.alt: Congo Basin rainforest along a winding river in southern Cameroon

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Rivers already give two thirds of the power; every new connection can be clean.
items.alt: A hydroelectric dam on the Sanaga River with power lines, Cameroon

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.
items.alt: A tall waterfall falling into a green forest gorge, Cameroon

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2024
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.
items.alt: Green tea fields on rolling highland hills, Cameroon

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 41.1% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.
items.alt: A busy street of Yaoundé on its green hills with people in the distance, Cameroon

items.name: KingsCombo Sarl
items.text: A Cameroonian maize enterprise that grows maize, makes maize products and offers training and consultancy to farmers; its founder was a 2025 finalist of the FAO mentorship programme for young agricultural producers in Africa.

items.name: upOwa
items.text: Sells solar home systems to off-grid households in Cameroon on a lease-to-own basis, with a deposit and monthly payments by mobile money, and counted nearly 28,000 active systems connecting nearly 140,000 people at 31 March 2023.

items.name: Mpokem Gaz
items.text: A Douala start-up that builds clean cooking stoves from salvaged sheet metal and cement, with a fan charged by a small solar panel, sold from FCFA 28,000 for a single burner.

items.name: Waspito
items.text: A Douala-based healthcare network for remote consultations and laboratory tests, with 100,000 paying clients, named among the Top 10 of Africa’s Business Heroes in 2025.

items.name: Efarm.cm
items.text: An online platform where Cameroonian farmers list their produce and receive marketing support to find buyers.

items.name: Advans Cameroun
items.text: A licensed microfinance institution at work since 2007 that lends to craftspeople, traders and smallholder farmers, its rural farm lending backed by a Proparco portfolio guarantee signed in January 2024.
